high: landfill_ops contradicts its own duty model: players may deliberately remove required covers and end the night even when sufficient material exists; lfNight validates only over-spending, so shirking can remain a successful tactic.

landfill_ops UI uses disabled cell buttons as an answer oracle. Illegal type/full placements cannot be attempted, making the implemented type_mismatch and cell_full feedback unreachable through normal UI and removing part of the required typed-intake judgment.
medium: gas_watch has a dominant reusable opening: checking calibration produces three distinct texts, so one fixed first check uniquely identifies every cause; the crossed-out cause display then exposes the answer state. Replay variation changes the label but rarely the diagnostic strategy.

Leachate treatment is represented only by an automatic one-unit nightly drain. Children manage exposure and tank capacity, but never make a treatment-operation judgment despite the profession text presenting treatment as part of the work.
low: curb_check permits completion after one incorrect bag decision and advances without requiring that case to be corrected, slightly weakening mastery of every-case judgment.

recommended_actions: Enforce maximum feasible daily covering in lfNight: when soil covers all exposed cells, require all; when short, require exactly soil-count covers. Disable night advancement until that duty is satisfied.

Keep placement buttons enabled for non-full cells and let lfPlace return visible type_mismatch/cell_full consequences, or otherwise conceal legality until commitment while preserving accessible feedback.
Rebalance gas evidence so no single fixed check separates all three causes; make at least two context-dependent checks necessary and avoid exact-text-driven answer elimination.
Give the player a small leachate-treatment decision, such as scheduling limited pump/treatment capacity against forecast risk.
On a curb mistake, require correction of the same bag or explicitly frame the unresolved bag as handed to a supervisor with a concrete cost.
